title: Tamsin and the Will
premise: Coral Halloran, a concierge at the Grand Verity Hotel who prides themselves on noticing what guests hide, receives a confession letter from a guest who died a week earlier — postmarked the day after his funeral. The letter claims the man, Aldous Wren, was murdered and points to a ledger 'hidden in plain sight' among the hotel's guest records, a cipher of room numbers and dates spanning thirty years. As Coral decodes the ledger, they discover it documents a chain of stolen inheritances, including their own family's lost estate — and that the killer, still a resident of the hotel, is watching them work. In the end Coral traps the murderer, Wren's estranged daughter, during a staged blackout in the ballroom, recovering the ledger and, with it, a version of their own history they never knew they'd lost.
about_author: Jonah Crane is the pen name of a former hotel night manager who spent eleven years watching strangers check in and out, collecting the small lies people tell at front desks. They write mysteries set in liminal places where identity is always negotiable.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Never Left
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Establishing Coral's gift for noticing guests' secrets at the Grand Verity, and their quiet loneliness. Aldous Wren, a longtime resident, dies alone in Room 412. Coral arranges the funeral details no family claims. Emotional beat: the ache of witnessing lives from the outside, never inside.

chapters.title: Postmarked After
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A week after the funeral, a letter arrives in Wren's handwriting, postmarked the day after he died: a confession that he was murdered, and a warning that the proof is 'in the book you file every day.' Coral's manager dismisses it as a prank. Emotional beat: vertigo — the dead speaking through the mundane.

chapters.title: Room 412, Sealed
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral visits the sealed room, finds Wren's belongings inventoried but one item missing: a leather folio he carried daily. A housekeeper mentions a woman visited the room before it was sealed, claiming to be family. Emotional beat: first flicker of danger beneath grief.

chapters.title: The Daughter at the Desk
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The woman, Vivian Ashe, checks into the hotel under her own name, charming and watchful. She asks pointed questions about Wren's mail. Coral, trained to read guests, reads her as someone performing normalcy. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing they may be the hunted.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Numbers
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral pulls thirty years of registration cards and finds Wren's pattern: room numbers and dates recorded on the backs of old folios, a cipher hiding in routine paperwork. First decoded entry points to a 1994 inheritance case. Emotional beat: the thrill of the code yielding, and dread at what it records.

chapters.title: What the Cipher Says
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The decoded entries reveal Wren documented a scheme of forged wills and stolen estates, brokered through the hotel for decades — with an accomplice still unidentified, marked only as 'V.' Coral realizes their own family name appears in the 1994 entry. Emotional beat: memory as betrayal; the past rewriting Coral's identity.

chapters.title: The Night Manager's Story
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: retired night manager Edda Kwan. Edda recalls Wren and a young lawyer, Victor Ashe, running 'estate services' from the hotel bar. Victor died years ago; his daughter Vivian inherited everything. Emotional beat: the hotel's long memory outliving its staff.

chapters.title: Vivian's Version
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. Vivian, grieving a father she resented, searches the hotel for the ledger Wren promised would clear her family's name — or damn it. She notices Coral watching her. Emotional beat: sympathy for the antagonist; two investigators circling the same truth.

chapters.title: Missing Pages
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Someone has been into the archives; the 1994 folio is gutted. Security footage shows Vivian's keycard — but the timestamp is impossible, during a staff meeting Coral attended. Someone is framing her, or her. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening like a ratchet.

chapters.title: The Detective Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A 'private investigator' named Mr. Latch interviews staff about Wren's death. Coral notices his shoes are hotel-issue slippers resoled — he's living in the building. Latch is the second hunter, and Coral can't tell whose side he's on. Emotional beat: trust becoming a liability.

chapters.title: Estate of Coral Halloran
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Digging into the 1994 entry, Coral learns the Halloran family farm was lost through a forged will — the first 'estate' Wren and Ashe processed. Coral's mother's signature is on the documents. Emotional beat: identity cracking open; belonging revealed as something taken.

chapters.title: Mother's Silence
chapters.summary: Coral visits their mother, who goes pale at Wren's name and admits she signed papers she never read, trusting a charming lawyer. She never told Coral because shame is easier than memory. Emotional beat: forgiveness beginning where anger can't reach.

chapters.title: Latch Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Latch corners Coral: he's hired by an anonymous client to recover the ledger before the estate settles. He offers Coral a share — and reveals he knows about the letter. Coral realizes the client must be inside the hotel. Emotional beat: the walls closing in, allies indistinguishable from threats.

chapters.title: The Bar at Closing
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. Vivian, desperate, breaks into Wren's sealed room and is caught by Coral. Instead of a fight, an uneasy alliance: she shows him her father's letters proving Wren was blackmailing Ashe, and she believes Wren's death was the blackmailee striking back. Emotional beat: enemies discovering a common wound.

chapters.title: Decoding the Last Entry
chapters.summary: Coral and Vivian, working through the night, crack the cipher's final layer: the ledger's location is encoded in the hotel itself — room numbers mapping to the lobby's brass mail slots, one slot never opened in thirty years. Emotional beat: the 'hidden in plain sight' promise fulfilled; hope with a timer on it.

chapters.title: Slot 412
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Behind mail slot 412: the ledger, complete, naming the surviving accomplice — not Ashe, but the hotel's own longtime solicitor, Mr. Penhale, who laundered the forgeries and killed Wren to bury the record. Coral photographs every page. Emotional beat: triumph curdling instantly — Penhale has access to everything, including them.

chapters.title: The Solicitor Smiles
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Penhale invites Coral to his office, all courtesy, and offers a quiet severance: leave, forget, and the Halloran estate papers will 'go missing' forever — Coral's heritage traded for silence. He mentions Coral's mother by name. Emotional beat: temptation and threat in one handshake.

chapters.title: What Coral Decides
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, night shift. Coral weighs the offer — the farm, the name, the belonging they've ached for — against the guests and staff who'd be next if Penhale stays free. Coral copies the ledger to three places and calls Edda Kwan home. Emotional beat: choosing identity over inheritance; selfhood claimed, not given.

chapters.title: The Blackout Gambit
chapters.summary: Coral, Vivian, and Edda stage a power failure during a hotel gala, forcing Penhale to retrieve his hidden originals from the safe in the dark. Coral, who knows the building's rhythms blind, waits in the archive corridor. Emotional beat: the watched becoming the watchers.

chapters.title: Ballroom, Candles
chapters.summary: Climax. Penhale takes the bait and is caught mid-theft by Vivian and Latch — who reveals he was hired by Wren himself, before his death, as insurance. Penhale, cornered, confesses to Wren's murder with the ballroom full of witnesses. Emotional beat: the confession letter's promise finally kept, publicly.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Aftermath: Penhale arrested, the Halloran estate claim filed with real lawyers this time, Vivian leaving with her father's cleared name. Coral declines to rush the farm's recovery — some things must be rebuilt slowly. Emotional beat: grief and justice settling like dust after a storm.

chapters.title: The Concierge Remembers
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, final. A new guest checks in, hiding something small and human, and Coral welcomes them with the same noticing kindness — but now for themselves too. The last line of Wren's letter, finally understood: 'The ledger was never the point. Someone had to see us.' Emotional beat: belonging found in witnessing, and being witnessed.
